statement: $return = shell_exec($command . " 2>&1 & ii=0 && while [ \"2\" -eq \"`ps -p $! | wc -l`\" ];do ii=$((ii+1)); if [ \$ii -gt ".($sec)."0 ]; then echo 'Intelmqctl timeout!';kill $!; break;fi; sleep 0.1; done");
cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: CWE-93 requires CRLF sequences to be used as special elements for line/record separation, and improper neutralization allows injection. The demonstrated mechanism is shell command execution with potential command injection, not CRLF-based record/line separation.

connection.evidence: User-controlled $_GET['action'] flows directly into $arguments when $scope == 'botnet' (line 36), then into $command via sprintf (line 124), then into shell_exec (line 131). No sanitization is applied to $action in botnet scope.

diff_causality.evidence: The candidate line adds a timeout wrapper to shell_exec. If reverted to the commented ExecWaitTimeout, the command execution remains but timeout mechanism changes. The injection vulnerability exists independently in the command construction logic (lines 25-113).

security_control.required_control: Neutralization of CRLF sequences when CRLF is used as a record separator
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-93 requires CRLF neutralization only when CRLF serves as a special element for line/record separation. No evidence shows CRLF is used as a separator in this shell command context.
security_control.deficiency_evidence: The botnet scope lacks any sanitization (line 36), but the deficiency is command injection, not CRLF injection. No evidence demonstrates CRLF sequences would be interpreted as command separators in this shell context.

concrete_impact.evidence: If unsanitized $action contains shell metacharacters, arbitrary command execution as intelmq user is possible. However, this is command injection impact, not CRLF injection impact. No evidence shows CRLF sequences would cause data modification or record separation issues.

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted to use ExecWaitTimeout instead of the shell_exec with inline timeout wrapper, the command execution vulnerability in botnet scope would remain unchanged, only the timeout implementation would differ.
supporting_evidence: User input $_GET['action'] flows directly into $arguments without sanitization when $scope == 'botnet' (line 36)
The constructed command is executed via shell_exec with sudo privileges
Other scopes use escapeshellcmd() or escapeshellarg() but botnet scope lacks any sanitization
contradicting_evidence: CWE-93 requires CRLF sequences to be used as special elements for line/record separation; shell commands use semicolons, ampersands, pipes, newlines, not specifically CRLF
The vulnerability mechanism is command injection via shell metacharacters, not CRLF injection affecting record boundaries
unresolved_facts: Whether the sudo -u intelmq configuration allows privilege escalation
Whether the timeout mechanism prevents command injection exploitation
Whether $_GET['action'] in botnet scope can contain shell metacharacters in practice
